sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Trafficking to plasma membrane confirmed by immunofluorescence with anti-myc antibody in non-permeabilized cells (surface-only labeling); tag demonstrated non-perturbative of PMP22 folding and trafficking across multiple studies; surface display in GPMVs confirmed by confocal fluorescence microscopy with anti-myc AF647.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 explicitly state the myc tag is inserted between residues 125 and 126 of human PMP22 in ECL2 (topology span 117–133). Python confirms seq[124]='H' and seq[125]='L', both ≥9 residues from TM boundaries (TM3 ends at 116, TM4 starts at 134). Multiple independent publications (L6–L14) corroborate the same ECL2 myc-tag construct with surface display and preserved trafficking/function. Full-length human PMP22 (NM_153321) with a 10-residue myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop (ECL2), expressed in stable inducible cell lines (pCW57.1 vector). Multiple independent studies confirm this exact junction in full-length, membrane-anchored human PMP22.

sources.claim: The 10-residue myc tag was inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop of PMP22, as this internal tag was previously demonstrated to be non-perturbative of PMP22 folding and trafficking ( Fig. 1 A ) ( 36 , 37 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Tag in this position neither affects the processing nor the trafficking of the protein (stated explicitly in L4); mouse PMP22 is a close ortholog of human PMP22.
sites.rationale: L3 and L4 report an HA tag in the second extracellular loop of mouse PMP22 (a close ortholog) in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct, with explicit statement that the tag does not affect processing or trafficking. No residue number is given, so the site is reported at region level (ECL2, spanning 117–133 in the human canonical sequence) without a pinned junction. This is ranked below the validated human myc-tag site at residue 125. Mouse PMP22 cDNA with an HA epitope tag inserted in the second extracellular loop (ECL2), expressed in full-length membrane-anchored form in the pCMX vector. The exact junction residue within ECL2 is not named in the cited text.

sources.claim: To make non-palmitoylated PMP22, a cDNA encoding the WT (wild-type) mouse protein with a human influenza HA (haemagglutinin) epitope tag sequence in the second extracellular loop in the pCMX vector was used as a template ( Tobler et al., 1999 ).

sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)

literature_notes: L1/L2 provide the strongest evidence: exact residue 125|126 junction in human PMP22 ECL2, validated in multiple independent studies (L6–L14) for surface display and preserved trafficking/function. L3/L4 add an independent HA-tag precedent in mouse ECL2 (indirect/ortholog), reported at region level only because no residue is named. L5 and L15 describe the N41Q glycosylation-deficient variant used to improve plasma-membrane trafficking efficiency; N41 is a glycosylation site in ECL1, not a tag insertion site, and no ledger line reports a tag inserted in ECL1. L16/L17 (C-terminal ALFA tag) and L18 (C-terminal GFP) are placed in other_positions because the PMP22 C-terminus (residues 157–160) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks (INTRACELLULAR: 157–160), making these cytoplasmic labels, not surface tags.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal ALFA tag on full-length PMP22 localizes to plasma membrane in HEK293T cells, but the C-terminus (residues 157–160) is intracellular per topology; this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
GFP fused to the PMP22 C-terminus used for co-immunoprecipitation; C-terminus is intracellular (topology: 157–160 INTRACELLULAR), so this is a cytoplasmic fusion, not a surface tag.
